chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Muhammad al-Razi, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever trims his nails on Saturday and on Thursday and removes hair from his moustache shall be cured from the pain of molars and the pain of the eye.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical benefit of trimming nails and shaving the moustache on Saturday and Thursday in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith links the specific days of Saturday and Thursday to physical well-being, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between spiritual discipline and bodily health. It highlights the Prophetic tradition of maintaining cleanliness (fitrah) as a means of warding off common ailments, specifically toothache and eye pain, thereby integrating daily hygiene with religious observance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-100 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hisan, on the authority of Abi Muhammad al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
Whoever cuts off his nails and shaves his moustache on Saturdays or Thursdays shall be immune from toothache and eye pains.”
